claims.statement: A renewable installer can plausibly secure pre/post meter consent, commissioning data, and a remediation protocol at the moment a heat-pump or PV retrofit is sold. The Commission explicitly includes digital controls among renovation measures, but neither exclusive data rights nor customer acceptance of an escrow product is yet evidenced.

The measurable loss is the weather-normalized gap between promised and observed post-retrofit energy cost or consumption. The Commission reports roughly 75% of EU buildings have poor energy performance and that deep renovation can materially reduce consumption, creating a large outcome to verify, while actual Polish performance-gap incidence remains unknown.

The first payer hypothesis is the installer or property owner using warranty, commissioning, or energy-service budget at retrofit acceptance; later payers could be lenders or insurers that need performance evidence. EU zero-emission-building policy supports the direction and bill-savings value, not the existence of a Polish underwriting budget.

contrary_evidence: The recast directive does not require existing buildings to be renovated to zero-emission level, so demand timing can remain slow.
Weather, occupancy, tariffs, and behavior make a simple savings guarantee easy to dispute.

economics.acquisition_route: Attach a read-only 12-month measurement-and-verification addendum to 10 new family-business installations, then ask one insurer or lender to review the evidence packet before offering any financial guarantee.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Verified multi-brand performance data could become a scalable underwriting and financing layer sold through installers across Central Europe; reaching the founder objective requires recurring portfolio fees rather than one-off audits.
economics.founder_time: About 10-15 hours per week for analytics, customer reporting, and partner design; installation and remedial visits stay with contractors.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Software measurement is high-margin after data ingestion, but any remediation reserve is a direct loss cost and must be separately priced and capped.
economics.payback: The pilot should recover sensor and onboarding cost within the first annual service fee; underwriting capital is deferred until a claims distribution exists.
economics.pricing: Fixed commissioning evidence fee plus monthly monitoring; optional capped performance protection priced as a percentage of installation value after loss data exists.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Monitoring renews annually and can extend to maintenance, tariff optimization, equipment replacement, and lender reporting.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Weather-normalized outcome and remediation data across installer brands, building types, and equipment
fingerprint.customer: Polish residential and small-commercial retrofit installers, property owners, and eventually lenders or insurers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embedded add-on at the installer quote and commissioning handoff
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Independent measurement, evidence escrow, and later capped performance protection sold per retrofit and per monitored year
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Installer or owner pays when a retrofit is commissioned; a protection payout is triggered by a defined verified shortfall
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A costly energy retrofit is sold on savings that neither party can cleanly verify after installation

founder_fit: The family company can supply a real installation cohort and commissioning workflow for a low-cost pilot.
Weather normalization, causal baselining, and anomaly detection fit the founder's data-science strengths.
The business can begin as evidence software without taking uncapped insurance risk.
risks: Offering a guarantee could constitute regulated insurance or create uncapped contractual exposure.
Meter access and clean pre-installation baselines may be unavailable.
Installers may resist independent evidence that can attribute underperformance to their work.

structure.control_point: The signed commissioning baseline, meter consent, and definition of a compensable shortfall
structure.critical_dependency: Reliable normalization plus a legally permissible risk-transfer partner for any guarantee

thesis: Backcast from a building market where finance follows measured operating performance rather than equipment labels: capture trusted baseline and commissioning evidence now through a local installer channel, then compound outcome data into underwriting power.
title: Retrofit Performance Escrow
uncertainties: Observed shortfall frequency and remediation cost across Polish heat-pump and PV installs are unknown.
It is unclear whether customers value neutral verification enough to pay separately.
A lender or insurer has not confirmed that this evidence changes approval, pricing, or claims handling.
